rv.q: This is a play about mental illness, and profoundly about identity… Like Kevin, it is as Irish as can be.
It also confirms Fortune as an actor worth watching and watching for.
The Black Wolfe Tone is an arresting and thought-provoking look into one man’s life.
Some of that comes across–but in a manner even more haphazard and undisciplined than the sad, excitable young chap delivering the details.

cn.t: Fortune delivers a powerful solo debut exploring race and mental health in modern Ireland, though the intense, claustrophobic experience divides critics between those moved by his commanding presence and those exhausted by the ordeal.
